prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universal “best” interior painter in St. Louis — the right company depends on your project (whole-house vs. single room, trim/ceiling work, level of prep/repairs), budget, timeline and whether you need specialized services (historic home, lead-safe work, color consulting). I can help you find the best match. Before I do that, here’s a quick guide to identify the best company for your situation and what to ask.

How to pick the best interior painting company
- Reviews & reputation: Check recent Google, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor reviews and Better Business Bureau rating. Look for consistent quality and how the company responds to complaints.
- Experience & portfolio: Ask to see recent interior jobs like yours (before/after photos).
- Licensing & insurance: Verify general liability insurance and worker’s comp. For homes built before 1978, ask about EPA Lead-Safe certification.
- Written estimate & scope: Get itemized, written estimates (prep work, number of coats, paint brand/finish, number of painters, timeline, clean-up).
- Warranty/guarantee: Ask what’s covered and for how long.
- Prep & materials: Confirm whether they include patching, sanding, priming, caulking, trim work, and whether they supply paint or you do (and which brands/lines they use).
- Communication & timeline: Confirm start date, work hours, and how they protect floors/furniture.
- References: Ask for 2–3 recent local references and follow up.

Questions to ask each company
- Are you insured and licensed? Can I see proof?
- Do you have EPA Lead-Safe certification (if applicable)?
- Who will supervise the job? Will you use subcontractors?
- How many coats of paint do you include and which brand/line?
- What prep work is included (patching, sanding, priming)?
- What is the estimated start and completion date?
- Do you provide a written warranty?

Red flags
- No written contract or vague scope
- Very low bid compared to others without explanation
- Poor or no references / no online presence
- Requests for large upfront cash payments
- No proof of insurance

Ballpark cost expectations (St. Louis area, ballpark only)
- One small room: $300–$800
- Average-sized room: $400–$1,200
- Whole interior of a typical 1,500–2,500 sq ft home: $3,000–$10,000+
Actual price depends on prep, ceiling/trim work, number of colors/coats, and paint quality.

Would you like me to:
- Research and list top-rated interior painting companies in your ZIP code?
- Prepare an email/template to request estimates from painters?
- Help you narrow choices based on budget, number of rooms, or special needs (historic home, lead-safe)?

Tell me your ZIP code, number of rooms or scope, and any priorities (budget, timeline, paint brand), and I’ll pull a short vetted shortlist and suggested questions for each.
